title: CBA dumps Qantas for Virgin in rewards rejig
full_text:
Commonwealth Bank has relaunched its credit cards rewards scheme, favouring Virgin Australia over Qantas as part of a major shake-up and expansion of its Yello spending scheme.
CBA said it was making changes to its credit card scheme, including launching Discover Card in Australia from October as the banking sector readjusts to the RBA’s changes to card surcharges.
The banking giant’s nine million customers will now be able to access its Yello rewards points, to use them on a multitude of spending options and on its platform. Customers will be able to earn points at a rate to be determined, through their CBA home loans, select transaction accounts, term deposits, as well as through buying insurance. Points will be able to be redeemed on fuel, groceries and travel credits.
Among those partnered with CBA on the relaunched scheme are Woolworths, Origin Energy, Myer, DoorDash, BP, Qatar Airways and Virgin’s Velocity frequent-flyer scheme.
The decision marks a stepping away from Qantas by CBA, which has traditionally provided Qantas points from its existing stable of credit cards.
The new cards will not directly provide Qantas points. However, existing cards will continue to provide Qantas points – albeit at a lower earn rate of half a point per dollar. Frequent Flyer points will continue to transfer automatically from these cards for opted-in members.
Under the new CBA rewards program, frequent flyers can opt to transfer Yello points to their Qantas account at a rate of three Yello for one frequent flyer point, but that will come with the sting of a $149-a-year participation fee.
Yello points earned through CBA products can be transferred to Velocity at a rate of 2.5 Yello to one Velocity point, with a 20 per cent bonus earn for the first six months. At this stage there is no transfer fee, but watch this space.
Velocity CEO Andrew Cleary said the tie-up would help members build up their points balance given CBA’s reach.
Although Velocity has suffered through a smaller network of airline and retail partners, Mr Cleary said there were more announcements in the pipeline that would benefit members. Points could also be redeemed with premium international carriers Qatar Airways and Singapore Airlines. “This is really important. For a long time, points earn in Australia when it came to banks was only about credit cards,” Mr Cleary said.
By expanding its rewards program, CBA is aiming to work around the Reserve Bank’s cut to interchange fees taking effect in October that will reduce the amount of money financial institutions have to spend on things such as airline loyalty programs.
Instead, it hopes customers will engage more directly with its own Yello rewards, with those who spend more with CBA moving up the tiers and getting more points per dollar spent in return.
Point Hacks editor-in-chief Brandon Loo said: “If you’re a diamond customer you earn 1.5 points per dollar; while entry-level customers earn just half a point per dollar.” CBA retail banking boss Angus Sullivan said the bank was tying earnings points to a “more substantial relationship”, rather than following what other banks had done and simply devaluing their existing rewards schemes. He said it gave customers “an opportunity to get more value rather than just having a devaluation experience on the back of what the RBA has done”. Qantas has closer relationships with other banks, such as ANZ, AMEX, NAB and Westpac, but CBA customers who still want to build their frequent-flyer points balance should not despair.
